thread:
emma: quick follow-up to the mux-loader RFC — sketching a concrete boundary we can implement in the next sprint. idea: a single loader that multiplexes transports (http/s3/gcs/sidecar) and formats (safetensors, pt, tar+chunk), exposes a tiny sync hot-path for immediate inference start, and then continues async hydration for the rest of layers/quant variants. thoughts?

jorge: +1 to single surface. main risk is coupling warmup logic with transport edge-cases. we should define a tiny sync ABI that is strictly limited (e.g. return first N layers or a seed cache handle). anything beyond that must be async.

lia: agreed. proposed quick ABI:
```
// sync hot-path (blocking, bounded time)
LoadSync(model_id, routes, seed_layers) -> {handle, fast_metadata, seed_weights}

// async hydration (returns immediately)
Hydrate(handle, policy) -> stream of events / progress
```
Seed_layers default = embedding + first K blocks. policy includes prefetch_budget, parity_mode (replicate/striping), quant_target.

arjun: important: prefetch_budget should be credit-based and per-request-group (not global) so small requests don't get starved by a big batch. also need a backpressure signal from runtime: if kvcache pressure high, slow hydration.

emma: @arjun yep. runtime->loader signals: {pressure_level, preferred_latency_slo} so loader can adapt prefetch aggressiveness and switch to lower-cost quant variant or fallback model variant. runtime-bot: noted event "loader:pressure-signal" schema pushed to docs.

jorge: another tradeoff: aggressive on-the-fly quantization during hydration saves storage but can spike CPU/GPU. Suggest quant steps be configurable per deployment tier (hosted vs dedicated). for Hosted default = pre-quantized; for Dedicated allow dynamic quantization with cgroups/limits.

lia: we also need deterministic shard placement semantics so warmup across replicas is coherent. suggestion: manifest contains canonical chunk ids + content-addressed blob ids. loader must provide ResolveChunk(chunk_id) -> [transport_url(s)] and a prefer_local hint. resolves can be cached in a small LRU.

emma: operational concern: when a requested chunk fails mid-hydration, loader should: 1) emit telemetry 2) try alternate transport(s) 3) if still failing and chunk is non-critical, keep serving degraded; if critical (e.g. first K layers) fail-fast. ops: any runbook suggestions?

ops: runbook: on chunk failure we 1) mark model instance degraded, 2) route new requests to fallback variant if available, 3) auto-schedule manifest integrity check job. keep alerts noisy only for repeated failures > 5m. include a "degraded_reason" tag in telemetry.

arjun: important edgecase — dedup across bundles. same embedding weights can be referenced by multiple models (shared base). loader should expose dedup_key for blobs so storage and network can be cached at transport layer. that will reduce warmup traffic.

lia: +1 on dedup_key. implementation note: dedup_key = content-addressed-hash + origin namespace. but we should allow ephemeral overrides for on-prem where org wants to force local copy.

emma: compatibility note: keep the loader ABI stable and minimal. allow feature-gates for new policies (quant-on-hydrate, progressive-delivery). we'll ship a shim that translates old manifest schemas to the new canonical manifest (manifest-v2).

jorge: testing strategy: unit tests for ResolveChunk and LoadSync boundedness (simulate slow transports), integration test with a fake transport that panics mid-stream, and e2e perf test for: cold-start latency (sync path only) and steady-state token cost (hydration background work accounted).

lia: proto for diagnostics events we'll emit:
```
loader.hydration.started {handle, model_id, seed_layers}
loader.hydration.progress {handle, chunk_id, bytes, transport}
loader.hydration.failed {handle, chunk_id, error, attempts}
loader.loadsync.latency {handle, ms}
```
Keep these lightweight.

arjun: migration plan: land loader-v1 behind feature-flag, enable for internal canary traffic and a small % of hosted traffic. fallback to current loader if LoadSync takes > X ms or Hydrate fails > Y% in first N minutes.

emma: action items: 1) lia write ABI PR with interface + events, 2) jorge add prefetch_credit docs + runtime signal schema, 3) arjun prototype dedup_key caching in sidecar transport, 4) ops produce runbook snippet and alert thresholds. i'll bake this into a short RFC addendum.

lia: I'll open the PR today and include a minimal mocked transport for tests. cc @emma @jorge

jorge: I'll draft the prefetch_credit API and a few simulation numbers (how credits affect tail latency vs cost).

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: planned canary enablement window requested: 2024-11-12 08:00-12:00 UTC.

emma: thanks all — this feels like a implementable scope for the sprint. :raised_hands:
